svg.title: The frame dies. The heap block does not.
svg.desc: Two panels of the same call shape. On the left, make_buf returns a pointer to a 32-byte heap block; the make_buf frame is crossed out but a green arrow shows the block still alive and now owned by main. On the right, c() returns the address of a local int z; the frame is crossed out in red and the pointer in main now aims at bytes the next call will reuse. Below, the measured stack budget and a struct-padding comparison of 24 versus 16 bytes.
svg.text: The frame dies. The heap block does not.
the block is fine. It is now main()'s problem.
Who calls free()? Write it in the docstring.
c() returned. z's 4 bytes were not erased -
they are simply no longer yours.
char a; long b; char c; = 24 B
long b; char a; char c; = 16 B
